questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: Under SA 200, the overall objective of the auditor in an audit of financial statements is to:

options.A: Provide absolute assurance that the financial statements contain no fraud or error of any amount
options.B: Certify the arithmetical accuracy of every transaction recorded in the books of account
options.C: Detect and prevent all frauds committed by employees and management during the year
options.D: Obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to report in accordance with the auditor's findings

questions.explanation: SA 200 frames the auditor's overall objective around reasonable assurance on the financial statements as a whole and reporting on the findings. Absolute assurance is not attainable because of the inherent limitations of an audit. Prevention and detection of fraud is primarily the responsibility of management and those charged with governance, and an audit does not verify every transaction.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: Reasonable assurance, as used in the Standards on Auditing, is best described as:

options.A: An absolute level of assurance obtained by testing all transactions
options.B: A moderate level of assurance expressed in negative form
options.C: A high, but not absolute, level of assurance
options.D: A low level of assurance sufficient only for internal use by management

questions.explanation: Reasonable assurance is a high but not absolute level of assurance, obtained when the auditor reduces audit risk to an acceptably low level. A moderate (limited) level of assurance expressed in negative form is characteristic of a review engagement, not an audit.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: Mr. Kunal, a trainee, lists the following as inherent limitations of an audit. Which one is NOT an inherent limitation recognised by SA 200?

options.A: Many financial statement items involve subjective judgements and estimates by management
options.B: The audit must be completed within a reasonable period and at a reasonable cost
options.C: The auditor has no legal power to compel third parties to provide information, as in a search
options.D: The auditor lacks the competence required to apply the Standards on Auditing

questions.explanation: SA 200 identifies inherent limitations arising from the nature of financial reporting (judgement and estimates), the nature of audit procedures (no legal powers of search, collusion, forgery) and the need for timeliness and cost balance. Lack of competence is not an inherent limitation; the auditor is expected to be competent, and accepting an engagement without competence would breach ethical requirements.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: Kamya Traders Ltd. asks its auditor to skip confirming a large receivable from an overseas customer because obtaining the reply would take time and add cost. No alternative procedure is available to obtain evidence on that balance. Per SA 200, the auditor should recognise that:

options.A: The procedure may be omitted if management gives a written representation on the balance
options.B: The procedure may be omitted provided the matter is mentioned in an Other Matter paragraph
options.C: The procedure may be omitted because the audit must balance cost against benefit
options.D: Difficulty, time or cost involved is not in itself a valid basis for omitting an audit procedure for which there is no alternative

questions.explanation: SA 200 accepts that an audit is subject to time and cost constraints, but states that difficulty, time or cost is not in itself a valid basis for omitting a procedure for which there is no alternative or for being satisfied with less than persuasive evidence. A written representation cannot replace evidence that is expected to be available, and an Other Matter paragraph does not cure a scope gap.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: Professional skepticism, as required by SA 200, includes:

options.A: Acceptance of management's explanations without corroboration where management has been honest in the past
options.B: A questioning mind, being alert to conditions that may indicate possible misstatement, and a critical assessment of audit evidence
options.C: A refusal to rely on any document provided by the entity
options.D: An assumption that management is dishonest unless proved otherwise

questions.explanation: Professional skepticism is an attitude that includes a questioning mind, alertness to conditions that may indicate misstatement due to error or fraud, and critical assessment of evidence. It neither assumes dishonesty nor unquestioning honesty. Past experience of honest management does not relieve the auditor of the need to maintain skepticism.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about professional judgment in an audit is correct?

options.A: It is needed only at the planning stage, when materiality is determined
options.B: It permits the auditor to depart from any requirement of an SA without documentation
options.C: It is exercised by the engagement team only after consulting management on each matter
options.D: It must be exercised throughout the audit and cannot be used to justify decisions that are not supported by the facts and circumstances of the engagement

questions.explanation: SA 200 requires the auditor to exercise professional judgment in planning and performing an audit, for example on materiality, audit risk, the nature, timing and extent of procedures and the evaluation of evidence. Judgment must be applied by a person with suitable training and experience, must be appropriately documented, and is not a justification for decisions unsupported by the facts.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: The managing director of Sitara Fabrics Ltd. states at a board meeting: 'Since our accounts are audited, any error in them is the responsibility of the auditor.' This view is:

options.A: Correct, because once the auditor signs the report the responsibility for the financial statements shifts to the auditor
options.B: Incorrect, because the responsibility lies solely with the shareholders who approve the accounts
options.C: Incorrect, because the audit of financial statements does not relieve management or those charged with governance of their responsibility for preparing the financial statements
options.D: Correct for errors but incorrect for frauds

questions.explanation: The preparation of financial statements in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework is the responsibility of management, with oversight by those charged with governance. The auditor's responsibility is to express an opinion on them. The audit does not relieve management of its responsibility, whether the misstatement arises from error or fraud.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: A lender asks Ms. Rhea, a practising Chartered Accountant, for a report on interim financial information in which she expresses a conclusion that nothing has come to her attention that causes her to believe the information is materially misstated. This is an example of:

options.A: An agreed-upon procedures engagement in which no assurance is expressed
options.B: A review engagement providing limited assurance expressed in negative form
options.C: An investigation, which provides absolute assurance on the information
options.D: An audit engagement providing reasonable assurance expressed in positive form

questions.explanation: A conclusion worded as 'nothing has come to our attention' is a negatively expressed conclusion, which is characteristic of a review engagement providing limited assurance. An audit gives reasonable assurance in the form of a positive opinion. In agreed-upon procedures, only factual findings are reported and no assurance is expressed.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: The directors of Vaanya Agro Ltd. instruct the statutory auditor not to verify inventory held at one of its five depots, stating that the depot manager is trustworthy. Inventory at that depot is material to the financial statements. Which statement best reflects the position of the auditor?

options.A: The scope of the audit is determined by the auditor under the SAs, the applicable law and the terms of engagement, and such a restriction is a management-imposed limitation that may lead to a modified opinion
options.B: The auditor should accept a written representation from the depot manager in place of verification and issue an unmodified opinion
options.C: The directors may lawfully restrict the scope of an audit, so the auditor should exclude the depot and issue an unmodified opinion
options.D: The auditor must immediately resign without communicating with those charged with governance

questions.explanation: The scope of an audit is set by the requirements of the SAs, relevant law and the terms of engagement, and management cannot curtail it. A management-imposed restriction over a material item is a limitation on scope; under SA 705 the auditor should request removal, communicate with those charged with governance and consider alternative procedures. If sufficient appropriate evidence still cannot be obtained, the opinion must be modified. A representation from an interested employee is not a substitute for the evidence.

questions.topic: Nature, Objective and Scope of Audit
questions.question_text: After an audit conducted in accordance with the SAs, it is discovered that the accountant and an outside supplier had colluded to raise forged invoices that looked genuine. The auditor had not detected the fraud. Which statement is most appropriate?

options.A: The subsequent discovery of a material fraud does not by itself indicate that the audit was not performed in accordance with the SAs, as the auditor is not expected to be an expert in authenticating documents
options.B: The auditor is automatically guilty of gross negligence because a material fraud remained undetected
options.C: The auditor is not responsible in any case because fraud detection is never an audit objective
options.D: The auditor should have physically verified every invoice with the supplier, as required by SA 500

questions.explanation: SA 200 and SA 240 recognise that fraud involving collusion and forgery may not be detected even in a properly planned and performed audit. A later discovery of fraud does not by itself mean the audit failed to comply with the SAs; the question is whether the auditor performed procedures appropriate in the circumstances with professional skepticism. Detecting material misstatement due to fraud is still within the auditor's objective, so the auditor is not exempt from responsibility.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: According to SA 300, the overall audit strategy:

options.A: Is the written agreement on the terms of the engagement signed by management
options.B: Is prepared only after the audit fieldwork is completed
options.C: Is a detailed list of procedures to be applied to each account balance
options.D: Sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit and guides the development of the audit plan

questions.explanation: SA 300 requires the auditor to establish an overall audit strategy that sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit, and that guides the development of the more detailed audit plan. The written agreement of terms is the engagement letter under SA 210, and a detailed list of procedures is the audit plan or programme.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a matter included in the audit plan rather than in the overall audit strategy?

options.A: The factors that are significant in directing the efforts of the engagement team
options.B: The reporting objectives of the engagement and the timing of the audit
options.C: The nature, timing and extent of planned further audit procedures at the assertion level
options.D: The characteristics of the engagement that define its scope, such as the reporting framework

questions.explanation: Under SA 300, the audit plan describes the nature, timing and extent of planned risk assessment procedures and further audit procedures at the assertion level. The scope-defining characteristics, reporting objectives and timing, and the factors directing the team's efforts are considered while establishing the overall audit strategy.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: Midway through the audit of Neelgiri Tea Ltd., the audit team learns that a major subsidiary has been sold. The engagement partner says the audit plan, once approved, cannot be changed. Under SA 300:

options.A: Planning is a continual and iterative process; the strategy and plan must be updated as necessary and significant changes, with reasons, documented
options.B: The change should be made but need not be documented because the final audit file shows the work done
options.C: The plan may be altered only with the written approval of the company's board of directors
options.D: The plan may not be altered, and the effect of the sale should be dealt with in the next year's audit

questions.explanation: SA 300 states that planning is not a discrete phase but a continual and iterative process. The auditor shall update and change the overall audit strategy and audit plan as necessary during the audit, and document significant changes and the reasons for them. Management approval is not required to change the auditor's plan.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: SA 300 requires which of the following persons to be involved in planning the audit?

options.A: The engagement quality reviewer alone
options.B: The engagement partner and other key members of the engagement team
options.C: The chief financial officer of the entity
options.D: Only the article assistants who will perform the fieldwork

questions.explanation: SA 300 requires the engagement partner and other key members of the engagement team to be involved in planning the audit, including discussions among team members. Their involvement brings experience and insight into the planning process. The client's CFO does not plan the audit, and the engagement quality reviewer has a separate, objective review role rather than planning the audit.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a preliminary engagement activity required at the beginning of the current audit engagement under SA 300?

options.A: Evaluating compliance with relevant ethical requirements, including independence
options.B: Establishing an understanding of the terms of the engagement as required by SA 210
options.C: Performing procedures regarding the continuance of the client relationship and the specific engagement
options.D: Performing tests of details on sales cut-off around the year-end

questions.explanation: SA 300 requires the auditor, at the beginning of the engagement, to perform the procedures required by SA 220 regarding continuance of the client relationship and the specific engagement, evaluate compliance with ethical requirements including independence, and establish an understanding of the terms of engagement (SA 210). Cut-off testing is a further audit procedure performed in response to assessed risks, not a preliminary engagement activity.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: Rajat & Co. has been appointed auditor of Jivika Ltd. for the first time. Which additional planning consideration applies specifically because it is an initial audit engagement?

options.A: Relying on the previous year's audit report as sufficient evidence for all opening balances
options.B: Reducing materiality to zero because the auditor has no past knowledge of the entity
options.C: Omitting the risk assessment for the first year because the predecessor already did it
options.D: Arranging, where permitted, to review the predecessor auditor's working papers and planning procedures for opening balances under SA 510

questions.explanation: SA 300 notes that in an initial audit the auditor may need to expand planning activities, including arrangements with the predecessor auditor to review its working papers and procedures required by SA 510 regarding opening balances. The predecessor's report alone is not sufficient evidence, and risk assessment cannot be skipped.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: An audit programme is best described as:

options.A: A summary of the client's accounting policies prepared by management
options.B: A list of the client's employees responsible for each ledger
options.C: A statement of the auditor's opinion issued at the end of the audit
options.D: A detailed plan of audit procedures that also serves as a set of instructions to assistants and a record of work performed

questions.explanation: An audit programme sets out the audit procedures to be performed. It instructs the assistants on the work to be done, helps allocate and control work, and when initialled serves as evidence of the work performed. It is prepared by the auditor, not management.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: Which of the following is generally regarded as a limitation of using a standard audit programme?

options.A: The work may become mechanical, and assistants may not look beyond the listed steps even when circumstances call for it
options.B: It removes the need for supervision and review of assistants' work
options.C: It makes it impossible to allocate work among assistants
options.D: It cannot be used as evidence of the work actually performed

questions.explanation: A common criticism of audit programmes is that they can make the work mechanical and discourage initiative, so that unusual matters outside the programme are missed. They help allocate work and evidence work done, but supervision and review are still required. Programmes should be reviewed and adapted to the circumstances.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: For the audit of Aranya Paints Ltd., the auditor selects profit before tax of Rs. 4.8 crore as the benchmark and applies 5% to determine materiality for the financial statements as a whole. Performance materiality is set at 75% of that materiality. What is performance materiality?

options.A: Rs. 18 lakh
options.B: Rs. 12 lakh
options.C: Rs. 24 lakh
options.D: Rs. 36 lakh

questions.explanation: Materiality = 5% x Rs. 480 lakh = Rs. 24 lakh. Performance materiality = 75% x Rs. 24 lakh = Rs. 18 lakh. Rs. 24 lakh is overall materiality, Rs. 36 lakh wrongly applies 7.5% to the benchmark, and Rs. 12 lakh applies 50%. SA 320 leaves the percentages to professional judgment; these are given in the question.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: Under SA 320, the main purpose of setting performance materiality at an amount lower than materiality for the financial statements as a whole is to:

options.A: Reduce to an appropriately low level the probability that the aggregate of uncorrected and undetected misstatements exceeds materiality for the financial statements as a whole
options.B: Ensure that every individual misstatement below performance materiality is ignored
options.C: Determine the threshold above which misstatements must be reported in the auditor's report
options.D: Replace the need for professional judgment in evaluating misstatements

questions.explanation: SA 320 explains that planning only to detect individually material misstatements ignores the fact that misstatements which are individually immaterial may add up to a material amount, together with undetected misstatements. Performance materiality is set below overall materiality to provide a margin for this aggregation risk. It does not mean smaller misstatements are ignored, and it is not a reporting threshold.

questions.topic: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
questions.question_text: At planning, the auditor of Dhruv Motors Ltd. set materiality at 1% of forecast revenue of Rs. 200 crore. Actual revenue for the year turns out to be Rs. 150 crore. Under SA 320, the auditor should:

options.A: Revise materiality to Rs. 1.5 crore but make no change to performance materiality or audit procedures
options.B: Continue with materiality of Rs. 2 crore because materiality is fixed at the planning stage
options.C: Revise materiality to Rs. 1.5 crore and determine whether performance materiality and the nature, timing and extent of further audit procedures remain appropriate
options.D: Revise materiality to Rs. 2.5 crore to reflect the shortfall in revenue

questions.explanation: Original materiality = 1% x Rs. 200 crore = Rs. 2 crore. Based on actual revenue, 1% x Rs. 150 crore = Rs. 1.5 crore. SA 320 requires the auditor to revise materiality when aware of information that would have caused a different amount initially. When the revised amount is lower, the auditor must reconsider performance materiality and whether the nature, timing and extent of further audit procedures remain appropriate.

questions.question_text: Audit risk is a function of:

options.A: Inherent risk and business risk only
options.B: Engagement risk and the auditor's fee
options.C: Control risk and sampling risk only
options.D: The risks of material misstatement and detection risk

questions.explanation: Audit risk is the risk that the auditor expresses an inappropriate opinion when the financial statements are materially misstated. It is a function of the risks of material misstatement (made up of inherent risk and control risk) and detection risk. Business risk is broader and only some of it gives rise to risks of material misstatement.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Prakash Chemicals Ltd. has assessed the risk of material misstatement for inventory valuation as high. The auditor should therefore:

options.A: Accept a higher detection risk because the inherent risk is already known
options.B: Accept a lower detection risk and obtain more persuasive audit evidence from substantive procedures
options.C: Lower materiality to zero for inventory and test every item without considering risk
options.D: Reduce substantive procedures and rely on management's representations

questions.explanation: Detection risk varies inversely with the assessed risk of material misstatement for a given level of audit risk. A high assessed risk requires a lower acceptable detection risk, which means more persuasive evidence through changes in the nature, timing and extent of substantive procedures, for example larger samples or procedures closer to the year-end.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the risk assessment procedures listed in SA 315?

options.A: Observation and inspection
options.B: External confirmation of trade receivable balances
options.C: Inquiries of management and other appropriate individuals within the entity
options.D: Analytical procedures

questions.explanation: SA 315 states that risk assessment procedures include inquiries of management and others, analytical procedures, and observation and inspection. External confirmation under SA 505 is generally used as a further audit procedure (substantive test) responding to assessed risks rather than as a risk assessment procedure.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Saanvi Realty Ltd. has identified revenue recognition on long-term contracts as a significant risk and plans to respond using only substantive procedures. Under SA 330, those procedures must:

options.A: Include tests of details
options.B: Be performed only at an interim date
options.C: Be limited to inquiries of the project managers
options.D: Consist only of substantive analytical procedures

questions.explanation: SA 330 requires that when the approach to a significant risk consists only of substantive procedures, those procedures shall include tests of details. Substantive analytical procedures alone are not considered sufficient for a significant risk, and inquiry alone never provides sufficient appropriate evidence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a component of internal control described in SA 315?

options.A: The information system and communication
options.B: The control environment
options.C: The entity's risk assessment process
options.D: The external audit function

questions.explanation: SA 315 describes the components of the entity's system of internal control as the control environment, the entity's risk assessment process, the information system (including related business processes) and communication, control activities, and monitoring of controls. The external auditor is independent of the entity and is not part of its internal control.

questions.question_text: At Ishaan Logistics Ltd., the stores keeper and the security guard together removed goods from the warehouse and prepared matching false gate passes. The controls were well designed but failed. This is an example of which inherent limitation of internal control?

options.A: Controls designed only for routine transactions
options.B: Collusion among two or more people
options.C: The cost of a control exceeding its benefit
options.D: Management override of controls

questions.explanation: Internal controls, however well designed, can be circumvented when two or more people collude, because segregation of duties relies on one person checking another. Here the stores keeper and guard acted together, defeating the control. Management override involves management, which is not the case.

questions.question_text: In Vritika Stores Pvt. Ltd., the cashier who receives cash from customers also posts entries to the customers' ledger accounts. This arrangement is weak because it:

options.A: Prevents the use of computerised accounting
options.B: Combines authorisation with execution of purchase orders
options.C: Violates the requirement that cash be banked daily
options.D: Combines custody of assets with recording of transactions, allowing misappropriation to be concealed

questions.explanation: Effective segregation of duties separates authorisation, recording and custody of assets. A cashier who also maintains the customer ledger can misappropriate receipts and conceal it by manipulating ledger entries, for example through teeming and lading. The weakness lies in combining custody with recording.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Harshil Steel Ltd. tested a control over credit approvals last year and found it effective. The control mitigates a significant risk. There is no change in the control this year. Under SA 330, the auditor intending to rely on it:

options.A: May rely on last year's test without further work, as the control has not changed
options.B: May rely on last year's test until the third audit, as permitted for all unchanged controls
options.C: Need only inquire of management whether the control has changed
options.D: Must test the operating effectiveness of the control in the current period

questions.explanation: SA 330 allows the auditor to use evidence from previous audits about unchanged controls, testing them at least once in every third audit. However, where the auditor plans to rely on controls over a risk that has been determined to be significant, the controls shall be tested in the current period. Inquiry alone is insufficient to test operating effectiveness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a test of control rather than a substantive procedure?

options.A: Obtaining a balance confirmation from a supplier
options.B: Recomputing depreciation charged on a sample of assets
options.C: Inspecting a sample of purchase orders for the signature of the authorised purchase manager
options.D: Comparing the year-end payables balance with an expectation based on purchases

questions.explanation: Tests of controls evaluate whether controls operated effectively, for example by inspecting documents for evidence of authorisation. Supplier confirmations, recomputation of depreciation and analytical comparison of payables are substantive procedures designed to detect material misstatements at the assertion level.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an application control in an IT environment?

options.A: An input check that rejects a sales order when the quantity field is left blank
options.B: A procedure requiring approval and testing before program changes are moved to production
options.C: Daily backup of data to an off-site data centre
options.D: A policy requiring users to change their passwords periodically

questions.explanation: Application controls operate at the level of individual applications and transactions, such as input validation, edit checks and matching. Password policies, program change management and backups are general IT controls that support the continued functioning of application controls across systems.

questions.question_text: During the audit of Mehar Textiles Ltd., the auditor identifies a deficiency in internal control that, in the auditor's judgment, is a significant deficiency. Under SA 265, the auditor shall:

options.A: Communicate it only if management has not already rectified it before the year-end
options.B: Communicate it in writing to those charged with governance on a timely basis, and also communicate it to management at an appropriate level
options.C: Communicate it orally to the accountant and record the discussion in the working papers
options.D: Disclose it in the Opinion section of the auditor's report

questions.explanation: SA 265 requires significant deficiencies to be communicated in writing to those charged with governance on a timely basis. They must also be communicated to management at an appropriate level, unless inappropriate in the circumstances. Other deficiencies of sufficient importance are communicated to management. Internal control deficiencies are not reported in the opinion paragraph under SA 265.

questions.question_text: The internal audit department of Kirat Foods Ltd. has tested inventory controls, and the statutory auditor decides to use this work under SA 610. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The external auditor retains sole responsibility for the audit opinion, which is not reduced by the use of the internal auditors' work
options.B: The external auditor must refer to the internal auditors' work in the auditor's report
options.C: Responsibility for the opinion is shared in proportion to the work done by the internal auditors
options.D: The external auditor may use the work without evaluating the objectivity or competence of the internal audit function

questions.explanation: SA 610 makes clear that the external auditor has sole responsibility for the audit opinion, and this is not reduced by using the internal audit function's work. The auditor must first evaluate the function's objectivity, competence and systematic and disciplined approach. The auditor's report does not refer to the internal auditors' work.

questions.question_text: An auditor uses the audit risk model AR = IR x CR x DR. Acceptable audit risk is 4%, inherent risk is assessed at 80% and control risk at 50%. What is the maximum acceptable detection risk?
questions.explanation: DR = AR / (IR x CR) = 0.04 / (0.80 x 0.50) = 0.04 / 0.40 = 0.10, or 10%. 8% results from ignoring inherent risk (0.04/0.50), 5% from ignoring control risk (0.04/0.80), and 1.6% from multiplying instead of dividing (0.04 x 0.40). A lower acceptable detection risk would call for more substantive work.

questions.question_text: Under SA 500, 'sufficiency' and 'appropriateness' of audit evidence refer respectively to:

options.A: The cost of obtaining evidence, and its relevance to management
options.B: The number of auditors involved, and the time spent on evidence
options.C: The quality of evidence, and the quantity of evidence
options.D: The quantity of evidence, and its quality in terms of relevance and reliability

questions.explanation: SA 500 defines sufficiency as the measure of the quantity of audit evidence and appropriateness as the measure of its quality, that is, its relevance and reliability in supporting the auditor's conclusions. More evidence does not compensate for poor quality evidence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following items of evidence is ordinarily the most reliable?

options.A: A photocopy of a bank statement provided by the accountant
options.B: A bank reconciliation statement prepared by the company's accounts team
options.C: A bank balance confirmation sent and received directly by the auditor
options.D: An oral explanation from the finance manager about the bank balance

questions.explanation: Evidence is generally more reliable when obtained from independent sources outside the entity, when obtained directly by the auditor, when in documentary form and when in original form. A confirmation received directly from the bank meets all these conditions. Photocopies, oral explanations and internally prepared documents are less reliable.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Oorja Electricals Ltd. selects goods dispatch notes issued in the last week of the year and traces them to sales invoices and the sales ledger. This procedure primarily tests which assertion for sales?

options.A: Classification
options.B: Occurrence
options.C: Completeness
options.D: Presentation

questions.explanation: Tracing from source documents (dispatch notes) to the accounting records tests whether all transactions that occurred have been recorded, which is the completeness assertion. Testing in the opposite direction, from ledger entries back to supporting documents, tests occurrence.

questions.question_text: The auditor selects entries from the purchases account and vouches them to supplier invoices and goods received notes. The primary assertion tested is:

options.A: Valuation of inventory
options.B: Completeness of purchases
options.C: Cut-off of sales
options.D: Occurrence of purchases

questions.explanation: Vouching from recorded entries back to supporting evidence checks that the recorded purchases actually took place and pertain to the entity, which is the occurrence assertion. It cannot detect unrecorded purchases, so it does not test completeness.

questions.question_text: Management of Tanvi Exports Ltd. refuses to allow the auditor to send a confirmation request to a major customer. Under SA 505, the auditor shall FIRST:

options.A: Accept the refusal and rely on a written representation about the balance
options.B: Immediately issue a disclaimer of opinion
options.C: Inquire into management's reasons for the refusal and seek audit evidence about their validity and reasonableness
options.D: Send the confirmation request anyway without informing management

questions.explanation: SA 505 requires the auditor to inquire as to management's reasons, seek evidence as to their validity and reasonableness, evaluate the implications for risk assessment including fraud risk, and perform alternative procedures. If the refusal is unreasonable or alternative evidence cannot be obtained, the auditor communicates with those charged with governance and considers the effect on the opinion under SA 705.

questions.question_text: SA 505 permits negative confirmation requests as the sole substantive procedure for an assertion only when certain conditions are all present. Which of the following is one of those conditions?

options.A: The recipients are likely to disregard the requests
options.B: The population consists of a large number of small, homogeneous account balances
options.C: A high exception rate is expected
options.D: The assessed risk of material misstatement is high

questions.explanation: Negative confirmations provide less persuasive evidence than positive ones. SA 505 allows them as the sole substantive procedure only where the risk of material misstatement is low and controls are tested, the population is a large number of small homogeneous balances, a very low exception rate is expected, and there is no reason to believe recipients will disregard them.

questions.question_text: When inventory is material, SA 501 requires the auditor to attend the physical inventory count, unless impracticable, in order to:

options.A: Take over the count from the client's staff and value the inventory personally
options.B: Sign the inventory sheets as a certificate of quantities and values
options.C: Ensure that the count is conducted only on the last day of the financial year
options.D: Evaluate management's instructions, observe the count procedures, inspect the inventory and perform test counts

questions.explanation: SA 501 requires attendance at physical inventory counting to evaluate management's instructions and procedures, observe their performance, inspect the inventory and perform test counts. The count remains management's responsibility. The count can be at a date other than the year-end, with procedures to cover movements in between.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Pankhuri Minerals Ltd. is unable to attend the inventory count at a remote mine because it is in an area declared unsafe due to flooding. Inventory there is material. Under SA 501, the auditor should:

options.A: Accept a certificate from the mine manager as conclusive evidence
options.B: Perform alternative audit procedures to obtain evidence on existence and condition, and modify the opinion under SA 705 if this is not possible
options.C: Issue an unmodified opinion because the reason for non-attendance is beyond the auditor's control
options.D: Withdraw from the engagement immediately

questions.explanation: Where attendance is impracticable, for example due to safety concerns, SA 501 requires the auditor to perform alternative procedures such as inspecting subsequent sales documents for specific items. If that is not possible, the auditor modifies the opinion under SA 705. A certificate from an interested official is weak evidence, and mere inconvenience does not justify non-attendance.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Riddhi Pharma Ltd. assesses a risk of material misstatement regarding pending litigation and wishes to communicate with the company's external legal counsel. Management refuses permission. Under SA 501, the auditor shall:

options.A: Modify the opinion in accordance with SA 705 if management refuses permission and alternative procedures do not provide sufficient appropriate evidence
options.B: Contact the counsel directly without management's permission
options.C: Report the matter to the Central Government
options.D: Rely on the management's internal legal department's list and issue an unmodified opinion

questions.explanation: SA 501 requires direct communication with external legal counsel through a letter of inquiry prepared by management and sent by the auditor where there is a risk of material misstatement. If management refuses permission, or counsel refuses to respond and alternative procedures do not provide sufficient evidence, the auditor shall modify the opinion under SA 705.

questions.question_text: Using monetary unit sampling on trade receivables of Rs. 6 crore, the auditor selects 120 items using a fixed sampling interval. One selected balance with a book value of Rs. 2,00,000 has an audited value of Rs. 1,50,000. What is the projected misstatement for this sampling interval?
questions.explanation: Sampling interval = Rs. 6,00,00,000 / 120 = Rs. 5,00,000. Misstatement = Rs. 2,00,000 - Rs. 1,50,000 = Rs. 50,000, so tainting = 50,000 / 2,00,000 = 25%. Because the item is smaller than the interval, projected misstatement = 25% x Rs. 5,00,000 = Rs. 1,25,000. Rs. 50,000 is only the actual misstatement, which SA 530 requires to be projected.

questions.question_text: The auditor tests a sample of inventory items with a book value of Rs. 40 lakh and finds an audited value of Rs. 38 lakh. Total inventory book value is Rs. 5 crore. Using ratio estimation, the projected misstatement for the population is:

options.A: Rs. 25 lakh overstatement
options.B: Rs. 50 lakh overstatement
options.C: Rs. 2 lakh overstatement
options.D: Rs. 20 lakh overstatement

questions.explanation: Misstatement in sample = Rs. 40 lakh - Rs. 38 lakh = Rs. 2 lakh, a ratio of 2/40 = 5%. Projected misstatement = 5% x Rs. 500 lakh = Rs. 25 lakh overstatement. Rs. 2 lakh ignores projection required by SA 530, Rs. 20 lakh uses 4%, and Rs. 50 lakh uses 10%.

questions.question_text: Swara Software Ltd. had 250 employees throughout the year, each paid Rs. 30,000 per month. A uniform 8% increment was given with effect from 1 October; the financial year ends on 31 March. Using a substantive analytical procedure, what is the auditor's expected annual salary cost? (Ignore other components.)

options.A: Rs. 9.72 crore
options.B: Rs. 9.00 crore
options.C: Rs. 9.18 crore
options.D: Rs. 9.36 crore

questions.explanation: Monthly cost before increment = 250 x Rs. 30,000 = Rs. 75 lakh; for April to September: 75 x 6 = Rs. 450 lakh. Monthly cost after increment = 75 x 1.08 = Rs. 81 lakh; for October to March: 81 x 6 = Rs. 486 lakh. Expected cost = 450 + 486 = Rs. 936 lakh, i.e. Rs. 9.36 crore. Rs. 9.72 crore applies the increment for the full year, Rs. 9.00 crore ignores it, and Rs. 9.18 crore applies it for only three months.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Ojas Infra Ltd. engages a valuer as an auditor's expert to value land. The auditor issues a qualified opinion relating partly to the land valuation and wishes to mention the expert. Under SA 620:

options.A: Reference to the expert transfers responsibility for the land valuation to the expert
options.B: The auditor may refer to the expert's work if relevant to understanding the modification, but must indicate that the reference does not reduce the auditor's responsibility for the opinion
options.C: The auditor must always name the expert in the auditor's report, whether or not the opinion is modified
options.D: The auditor may never refer to an expert in any auditor's report

questions.explanation: SA 620 states that the auditor has sole responsibility for the opinion, which is not reduced by the use of an auditor's expert. In an unmodified report, the auditor shall not refer to the expert unless required by law or regulation. If reference is made because it is relevant to understanding a modification, the report must state that the reference does not reduce the auditor's responsibility.

questions.question_text: During the audit of Chaitra Retail Ltd., the auditor finds a significant transaction with an entity controlled by a director's spouse, which management had not disclosed as a related party. Under SA 550, the auditor shall:

options.A: Ignore it because identifying related parties is solely management's responsibility
options.B: Record it in the working papers but take no further action as long as the amount is at arm's length
options.C: Promptly communicate the information to the engagement team, request management to identify all such transactions, and reconsider the risk of other undisclosed related parties
options.D: Report it immediately to the Registrar of Companies

questions.explanation: SA 550 requires the auditor, on identifying previously unidentified or undisclosed related parties or significant related party transactions, to communicate this to the engagement team, request management to identify all such transactions, inquire why controls failed, perform appropriate substantive procedures and reconsider the risk that other related parties exist. If non-disclosure appears intentional, the auditor evaluates the implications for the audit.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: Goods were dispatched to a customer of Lavanya Ceramics Ltd. on 31 March (the year-end) with control passing on dispatch, but the invoice was raised on 2 April. Which procedure best detects such an error?

options.A: Recomputing the GST payable for the month of March
options.B: Reviewing the minutes of the annual general meeting
options.C: Examining dispatch records for a few days before and after the year-end and matching them with the period in which sales were recorded
options.D: Obtaining a confirmation of the bank balance as on 31 March

questions.explanation: This is a sales cut-off issue. Revenue should be recognised in the period in which control passed, i.e. March. Cut-off testing involves matching dispatch documents around the year-end with the period of recording to ensure sales are recorded in the correct period. Bank confirmations and AGM minutes do not address this.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: The auditor of Bhoomi Engineering Ltd. selects assets physically present on the factory floor and traces them to the fixed asset register. This procedure primarily provides evidence about:

options.A: Valuation of property, plant and equipment
options.B: Occurrence of depreciation expense
options.C: Existence of property, plant and equipment
options.D: Completeness of property, plant and equipment

questions.explanation: Tracing from physical assets to the register checks whether assets that exist are recorded, which tests completeness. Selecting items from the register and verifying them physically tests existence. Neither procedure on its own tests valuation.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: Title deeds of a factory building owned by Yatin Polymers Ltd. are lodged with a bank as security for a term loan. To verify title, the auditor should:

options.A: Obtain a certificate directly from the bank confirming that it holds the title deeds on behalf of the company
options.B: Accept a photocopy of the title deed certified by the company secretary
options.C: Disregard verification because the bank has already checked the title
options.D: Accept the company's own register of immovable properties as sufficient

questions.explanation: When title deeds are held by a lender as security, the auditor should obtain a confirmation directly from the bank that it holds the deeds, and examine the deeds where possible. The auditor should also check whether the property stands in the company's name and whether the charge is disclosed. Internal copies or registers are less reliable.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: Ekam Packaging Ltd. bought a machine on 1 October for Rs. 48 lakh. Its estimated residual value is Rs. 3 lakh and useful life 9 years. The company uses the straight-line method and charged Rs. 5 lakh as depreciation for the year ending 31 March. What should the depreciation for the year be?

options.A: Rs. 5.33 lakh
options.B: Rs. 2.5 lakh
options.C: Rs. 5 lakh
options.D: Rs. 2.67 lakh

questions.explanation: Annual depreciation = (Rs. 48 lakh - Rs. 3 lakh) / 9 = Rs. 5 lakh. The machine was used for 6 months (October to March), so depreciation = Rs. 5 lakh x 6/12 = Rs. 2.5 lakh. The company has overstated depreciation by Rs. 2.5 lakh. Rs. 2.67 lakh ignores residual value (48/9 x 6/12), and Rs. 5.33 lakh ignores both residual value and the time factor.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: The auditor of Garima Distributors Ltd. examines cash received from customers in the six weeks after the year-end and matches it to year-end receivable balances. This procedure provides evidence mainly about:

options.A: Existence and valuation (recoverability) of trade receivables
options.B: Classification of share capital
options.C: Occurrence of purchases
options.D: Completeness of trade payables

questions.explanation: Subsequent receipts against year-end balances show that the debts existed and were recoverable, supporting existence and valuation. Balances that remain unpaid long after the year-end may need an allowance for expected credit losses. The procedure says nothing about payables, purchases or share capital.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: Ritam Chemicals Ltd. holds 1,000 units of a product at a cost of Rs. 600 per unit. The expected selling price is Rs. 650 per unit and estimated costs necessary to make the sale are Rs. 80 per unit. At what amount should this inventory be carried?
questions.explanation: Net realisable value = Rs. 650 - Rs. 80 = Rs. 570 per unit. Inventory is valued at the lower of cost (Rs. 600) and NRV (Rs. 570), so Rs. 570 x 1,000 = Rs. 5,70,000. A write-down of Rs. 30,000 is required. Rs. 6,00,000 is cost, Rs. 6,50,000 is selling price, and Rs. 5,20,000 wrongly deducts costs to sell from cost.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: In verifying cash in hand of Uday Hotels Ltd. at several counters, which of the following is NOT good audit practice?

options.A: Counting cash at all locations simultaneously, or sealing cash not counted immediately
options.B: Allowing each cashier to count the cash in the auditor's absence and later obtaining a signed certificate of the amount
options.C: Carrying out surprise counts in addition to the count at the year-end
options.D: Conducting counts in the presence of the cashier and obtaining the cashier's signature on the count sheet

questions.explanation: The auditor should personally count or observe the count, in the cashier's presence, with simultaneous counts or sealing to prevent shifting of cash between locations, and should consider surprise counts. Relying on a cashier's certificate prepared without the auditor's observation provides weak evidence and defeats the purpose of physical verification.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: At year-end, Tejas Builders Ltd. recorded cheques of Rs. 60 lakh as issued to suppliers, reducing both the bank balance and trade payables. The auditor finds the cheques were actually handed over to suppliers only in the third week of the next month. The appropriate audit view is that:

options.A: The amount should be shown as a contingent liability in the notes
options.B: Only the bank balance should be increased by Rs. 60 lakh, with no change in payables
options.C: The cheques were not issued at the year-end; the payments should be reversed, increasing both the bank balance and trade payables by Rs. 60 lakh
options.D: The entries are correct because the cheques were written before the year-end

questions.explanation: A payment by cheque occurs when the cheque is delivered to the payee. Writing cheques but holding them back is a form of window dressing that reduces reported liabilities and improves ratios. The entries should be reversed so that both cash at bank and trade payables increase by Rs. 60 lakh; the auditor should also consider the implications for management integrity.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: While verifying share capital issued during the year by Pranav Textiles Ltd., the auditor should examine:

options.A: Board and general meeting minutes, the register of members, and the return of allotment filed with the Registrar
options.B: The fixed asset register and depreciation schedule
options.C: Only the cash book entries showing receipt of application money
options.D: The sales register and dispatch notes

questions.explanation: Verification of share capital involves checking authorisation in the memorandum and resolutions, minutes approving allotment, the register of members, receipt of money in the bank, and filings such as the return of allotment with the Registrar. The cash book alone does not show that shares were properly authorised and allotted.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: Saakshi Steels Ltd. has breached a covenant in its long-term loan agreement on or before the year-end, making the loan repayable on demand, and has not obtained a waiver by the year-end. This primarily affects which aspect of the borrowing that the auditor must verify?

options.A: Occurrence of interest expense
options.B: Completeness of share capital
options.C: Classification of the loan as a current liability
options.D: Existence of the lender

questions.explanation: Where a covenant breach on or before the reporting date makes a long-term liability payable on demand and no waiver exists at the reporting date, the liability is generally required to be classified as current. The auditor should review loan agreements, compliance with covenants and lender confirmations to ensure correct classification and disclosure.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: The auditor of Nandan Security Services Ltd. suspects that the payroll includes 'ghost' employees. Which procedure is most effective in addressing this risk?

options.A: Comparing the payroll with personnel records and attendance, and checking for duplicate bank account numbers of employees
options.B: Comparing total salary cost with the previous year
options.C: Checking that salary is debited to the correct expense account
options.D: Recomputing the total of the payroll register

questions.explanation: Ghost employees are fictitious names on the payroll. Matching payroll to independent HR records and attendance, and looking for several employees paid into the same bank account, directly addresses this risk. Casting the register, overall comparisons and posting checks would not identify fictitious individuals.

questions.topic: Audit of Items of Financial Statements
questions.question_text: Which procedure is most effective in identifying unrecorded contingent liabilities of Arjun Logistics Ltd.?

options.A: Reviewing minutes of board meetings, correspondence with lawyers and legal expense ledgers, and sending letters of inquiry to the company's external legal counsel
options.B: Vouching recorded provisions to supporting calculations
options.C: Obtaining confirmations from trade receivables
options.D: Recomputing the balance of the provisions account

questions.explanation: Contingent liabilities, by their nature, are often not recorded, so the auditor must look for evidence of them in sources such as minutes, legal correspondence, legal fees and letters to external counsel (SA 501). Vouching or recomputing recorded provisions tests existence or accuracy of recorded items, not completeness of unrecorded ones.

questions.question_text: Under SA 230, audit documentation primarily provides:

options.A: A substitute for the entity's own accounting records
options.B: A document for the client to use in preparing the financial statements
options.C: Evidence that management has complied with all laws
options.D: Evidence of the auditor's basis for a conclusion about achieving the overall objectives, and evidence that the audit was planned and performed in accordance with the SAs and applicable legal requirements

questions.explanation: SA 230 states that audit documentation provides evidence of the basis for the auditor's conclusion and evidence that the audit was planned and performed in accordance with the SAs and legal and regulatory requirements. It also helps direct, supervise and review the work. It is not a substitute for the entity's records.

questions.question_text: The audit working papers prepared during the audit of Ananya Foods Ltd. are the property of:

options.A: The Registrar of Companies
options.B: The shareholders of the company
options.C: The company
options.D: The auditor

questions.explanation: Working papers are the property of the auditor. The auditor may, at his discretion, make portions of them available to the entity, provided this does not undermine the independence or validity of the audit. The client has no right of ownership over them.

questions.question_text: The assembly of the final audit file after the date of the auditor's report is an administrative process. An appropriate time limit within which to complete it is ordinarily:

options.A: Not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor's report
options.B: Before the date of the auditor's report
options.C: Not more than 7 days after the date of the auditor's report
options.D: Any time before the next year's audit begins

questions.explanation: SA 230 requires the auditor to assemble the audit documentation in an audit file and complete the administrative process on a timely basis after the date of the report. The application material to SA 230 indicates that an appropriate time limit is ordinarily not more than 60 days after the date of the auditor's report. Firms build this limit into their quality control (quality management) policies. No new audit procedures are performed and no new conclusions are drawn during assembly.

questions.question_text: After the assembly of the final audit file of Kesar Exports Ltd. is complete, an audit manager wants to remove a working paper. Under SA 230:

options.A: The auditor shall not delete or discard documentation of any nature before the end of its retention period
options.B: Working papers can be removed once the client has adopted the financial statements
options.C: Only working papers relating to immaterial areas can be removed
options.D: Working papers can be removed if the engagement partner approves

questions.explanation: SA 230 prohibits deleting or discarding audit documentation of any nature after assembly of the final file and before the end of the retention period. If modifications or additions are necessary, the auditor documents the specific reasons, when and by whom they were made and reviewed.

questions.question_text: SA 230 requires audit documentation to be sufficient to enable whom to understand the nature, timing and extent of procedures performed, the results and evidence obtained, and significant matters and conclusions?

options.A: The client's board of directors
options.B: An experienced auditor having no previous connection with the audit
options.C: A new article assistant joining the firm
options.D: Any member of the public

questions.explanation: SA 230 sets the 'experienced auditor' test: documentation should enable an experienced auditor, with no previous connection to the audit, to understand the work performed, the evidence obtained and the significant matters and conclusions. An experienced auditor understands audit processes, SAs, the business environment and relevant reporting issues.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would ordinarily be kept in the permanent audit file rather than the current file?

options.A: The bank reconciliation working paper for the current year-end
options.B: The current year's lead schedule for trade receivables
options.C: Confirmation replies received for the current year
options.D: Copies of the memorandum and articles of association and long-term contracts

questions.explanation: The permanent file contains information of continuing importance to future audits, such as constitutional documents, long-term agreements, organisation charts and accounting manuals. The current file holds working papers relating to the current year's audit, such as reconciliations, lead schedules and confirmations.

questions.question_text: After the auditor's report for Ved Polymers Ltd. was dated, the auditor learns of a fact that existed at that date and performs new audit procedures, reaching new conclusions. Under SA 230, the auditor shall document:

options.A: Only the revised conclusion, replacing the earlier working papers
options.B: Nothing, because documentation cannot be changed after the report is dated
options.C: Only a note that the matter was discussed with management
options.D: The circumstances encountered, the new or additional procedures performed, evidence obtained and conclusions, and when and by whom the changes were made and reviewed

questions.explanation: SA 230 requires that in exceptional circumstances where the auditor performs new or additional procedures or reaches new conclusions after the report date, the auditor documents the circumstances, the procedures, evidence and conclusions and their effect on the report, and when and by whom the resulting changes were made and reviewed. Existing documentation is not replaced.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is ordinarily NOT required to be included in audit documentation under SA 230?

options.A: How the auditor addressed information inconsistent with a final conclusion on a significant matter
options.B: Identifying characteristics of the specific items tested
options.C: Superseded drafts of working papers and notes reflecting incomplete or preliminary thinking
options.D: Discussions of significant matters with management, including when and with whom

questions.explanation: SA 230 states that the auditor need not include superseded drafts of working papers or financial statements, notes reflecting incomplete or preliminary thinking, previous copies of documents corrected for typographical errors, and duplicates. Significant discussions, identifying characteristics of items tested and treatment of inconsistent information must be documented.

questions.question_text: In documenting the nature, timing and extent of audit procedures performed, SA 230 requires the auditor to record:

options.A: Only the name of the engagement partner who signed the report
options.B: The fee charged for each area of the audit
options.C: Who performed the work and the date it was completed, and who reviewed it and the date and extent of review
options.D: The personal opinions of team members about management

questions.explanation: SA 230 requires documentation of who performed the audit work and the date it was completed, and who reviewed the work and the date and extent of that review, along with identifying characteristics of items tested. This enables accountability and evidences supervision and review.

questions.question_text: Kanak Traders Ltd. closes its accounts on 31 March. In May, before the financial statements are approved, a major customer is declared insolvent; its financial position had been deteriorating for months before the year-end. Under SA 560 this is:

options.A: An event indicating conditions that arose after the year-end, requiring only disclosure
options.B: An event that has no relevance to the financial statements
options.C: An event providing evidence of conditions that existed at the year-end, requiring adjustment of the financial statements
options.D: An event that should be dealt with only in the next year's financial statements

questions.explanation: SA 560 distinguishes events that provide evidence of conditions existing at the period end (adjusting) from those indicative of conditions arising after it (non-adjusting). The customer's insolvency confirms that the receivable was impaired at the year-end, so the allowance for credit losses should be adjusted.

questions.question_text: A fire destroyed a warehouse of Ojasvi Furnishings Ltd. on 20 April, after the 31 March year-end and before the financial statements were approved. The loss is material. The appropriate treatment is:

options.A: No disclosure because the event occurred after the year-end
options.B: Disclosure of the nature of the event and an estimate of its financial effect, without adjusting the year-end figures
options.C: Adjustment of the inventory and PPE balances as at 31 March
options.D: A qualified audit opinion, regardless of disclosure

questions.explanation: The fire is a condition that arose after the reporting date, so it is a non-adjusting event. If material, its nature and estimated financial effect should be disclosed. The auditor evaluates whether disclosure is adequate; a properly disclosed non-adjusting event does not require a qualified opinion, though the auditor may consider an Emphasis of Matter paragraph.

questions.question_text: After the date of the auditor's report but before the financial statements are issued, the auditor of Ira Cosmetics Ltd. becomes aware of a fact that might have caused the report to be amended. Under SA 560, the auditor shall:

options.A: Immediately withdraw the report and resign from the engagement
options.B: Ignore it, because the auditor has no obligation after the report is dated
options.C: Discuss the matter with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, determine whether the financial statements need amendment, and inquire how management intends to address it
options.D: Perform a full re-audit of all balances before taking any other action

questions.explanation: SA 560 states that the auditor has no obligation to perform procedures after the report date, but if a fact becomes known that might have caused amendment, the auditor shall discuss it with management and TCWG, determine whether the financial statements need amendment and, if so, inquire how management intends to address the matter in the financial statements.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT ordinarily an event or condition that may cast significant doubt on an entity's ability to continue as a going concern under SA 570?

options.A: Net liability or net current liability position
options.B: A significant increase in the entity's market share
options.C: Loss of key management without replacement
options.D: Fixed-term borrowings approaching maturity without realistic prospects of renewal or repayment

questions.explanation: SA 570 lists financial, operating and other indicators such as net liability positions, maturing borrowings without prospects of renewal, adverse key ratios, loss of key management, loss of a major market and non-compliance with capital requirements. An increase in market share is ordinarily a positive indicator and does not by itself cast doubt on going concern.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Ruhan Airlines Ltd. concludes that the use of the going concern basis is appropriate but a material uncertainty exists, and management has made adequate disclosure. Under SA 570, the auditor shall:

options.A: Express a qualified opinion because a material uncertainty exists
options.B: Express an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph on going concern
options.C: Express an unmodified opinion and include a separate section headed 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'
options.D: Express an adverse opinion because the entity may fail

questions.explanation: Under the revised SA 570, where the going concern basis is appropriate, a material uncertainty exists and disclosure is adequate, the auditor expresses an unmodified opinion and includes a separate section with the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'. An Emphasis of Matter paragraph is not used for this purpose.

questions.question_text: In the case of Ruhan Airlines Ltd., suppose instead that a material uncertainty about going concern exists but management refuses to disclose it adequately in the financial statements. The auditor shall express:

options.A: A qualified or adverse opinion, as appropriate, and explain in the Basis for Opinion section that a material uncertainty exists that is not adequately disclosed
options.B: An unmodified opinion with a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section
options.C: An unmodified opinion with an Other Matter paragraph
options.D: A disclaimer of opinion in all cases

questions.explanation: SA 570 requires that if adequate disclosure about a material uncertainty is not made, the auditor shall express a qualified or adverse opinion as appropriate under SA 705. The Basis for Opinion section states that a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt and that the financial statements do not adequately disclose it.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Sahil Mills Ltd. concludes that the company has decided to cease operations, yet the financial statements have been prepared on a going concern basis. Under SA 570, the auditor shall:

options.A: Express a qualified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
options.B: Express an adverse opinion
options.C: Express an unmodified opinion with a Material Uncertainty section
options.D: Express an unmodified opinion because the basis of preparation is management's choice

questions.explanation: SA 570 provides that if the financial statements have been prepared using the going concern basis but, in the auditor's judgment, management's use of that basis is inappropriate, the auditor shall express an adverse opinion. The effect is both material and pervasive since every item is measured on an inappropriate basis.

questions.question_text: Under SA 580, written representations from management should be dated:

options.A: On the last day of the financial year
options.B: On any date after the auditor's report, before the AGM
options.C: As near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report
options.D: On the date of the engagement letter

questions.explanation: SA 580 requires written representations to be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report, and to be in the form of a representation letter addressed to the auditor. They must cover all financial statements and periods referred to in the report.

questions.question_text: During the audit of Zubin Agencies Ltd., the auditor concludes there is sufficient doubt about the integrity of management that its written representation on its responsibility for preparing the financial statements is not reliable. Under SA 580, the auditor shall:

options.A: Obtain an oral representation instead and issue an unmodified opinion
options.B: Issue an unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
options.C: Disclaim an opinion on the financial statements
options.D: Issue a qualified opinion limited to the areas affected

questions.explanation: SA 580 requires the auditor to disclaim an opinion under SA 705 if the auditor concludes that there is sufficient doubt about management's integrity such that the representations about management's fundamental responsibilities are not reliable, or if management does not provide those representations. The effect is considered pervasive.

questions.question_text: Under SA 450, the auditor shall accumulate misstatements identified during the audit, other than those that are:

options.A: Judgmental in nature
options.B: Identified by the internal auditor
options.C: Below performance materiality
options.D: Clearly trivial

questions.explanation: SA 450 requires accumulation of all misstatements identified during the audit other than those that are clearly trivial. Clearly trivial is a much smaller threshold than performance materiality. Judgmental and projected misstatements must also be accumulated and evaluated.

questions.question_text: Materiality for Kavya Sweets Ltd. is Rs. 50 lakh. Uncorrected misstatements, all overstating profit, are: factual Rs. 18 lakh, judgmental Rs. 14 lakh and projected Rs. 12 lakh. Which conclusion is most appropriate under SA 450?

options.A: Aggregate uncorrected misstatements are Rs. 44 lakh, which is material, so the opinion must be qualified
options.B: Aggregate uncorrected misstatements are Rs. 44 lakh; they are below materiality, but the auditor should consider whether the risk of undetected misstatements could take the total above materiality
options.C: Aggregate uncorrected misstatements are only Rs. 18 lakh, since only factual misstatements are considered
options.D: Aggregate uncorrected misstatements are Rs. 32 lakh, since projected misstatements are excluded

questions.explanation: Aggregate = 18 + 14 + 12 = Rs. 44 lakh, which is below materiality of Rs. 50 lakh. SA 450 requires factual, judgmental and projected misstatements to be considered together. Since the total is close to materiality, the auditor should consider the risk that undetected misstatements, together with these, exceed materiality, and may need to perform more procedures or request management to correct them.

questions.question_text: Under SA 520, analytical procedures performed near the end of the audit are designed to:

options.A: Assist the auditor in forming an overall conclusion as to whether the financial statements are consistent with the auditor's understanding of the entity
options.B: Determine the audit fee for the next year
options.C: Identify the risk assessment procedures to be performed
options.D: Replace all substantive tests of details performed earlier

questions.explanation: SA 520 requires the auditor to design and perform analytical procedures near the end of the audit that assist in forming an overall conclusion on whether the financial statements are consistent with the auditor's understanding. If they identify a previously unrecognised risk, the auditor revises the risk assessment and planned procedures.

questions.question_text: Under SA 700, the auditor expresses an unmodified opinion when:

options.A: The entity has earned a profit during the year
options.B: Management has provided all written representations, regardless of misstatements found
options.C: The auditor concludes that the financial statements are prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework
options.D: The financial statements contain no misstatement of any amount

questions.explanation: SA 700 requires an unmodified opinion when the auditor concludes that the financial statements are prepared in all material respects in accordance with the applicable framework. Immaterial misstatements may exist. Profitability and representations alone do not determine the type of opinion.

questions.question_text: Under SA 700, which section of the auditor's report must immediately follow the Opinion section?

options.A: Basis for Opinion
options.B: Responsibilities of Management for the Financial Statements
options.C: Key Audit Matters
options.D: Other Matter

questions.explanation: SA 700 requires the Opinion section to be presented first, followed directly by the Basis for Opinion section. Other sections, such as Key Audit Matters (where applicable) and the responsibilities of management and the auditor, follow later.

questions.question_text: SA 701 on communicating Key Audit Matters applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements of:

options.A: Listed entities, and other entities where the auditor decides to or is required by law or regulation to communicate key audit matters
options.B: All entities without exception
options.C: Only government companies
options.D: Only private companies with borrowings from banks

questions.explanation: SA 701 applies to audits of complete sets of general purpose financial statements of listed entities, and in circumstances where the auditor otherwise decides to communicate KAMs or is required by law or regulation to do so. Key audit matters are selected from matters communicated with those charged with governance.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Ilesh Power Ltd., a listed company, has decided to qualify the opinion on account of an unrecorded provision. Regarding the Key Audit Matters section, SA 701 provides that:

options.A: No KAM section is required once any opinion is modified
options.B: The matter giving rise to the qualified opinion is not described in the KAM section, since communicating KAMs is not a substitute for a modified opinion
options.C: The KAM section replaces the need for a Basis for Qualified Opinion section
options.D: The matter must be described both in the KAM section and in the Basis for Qualified Opinion section

questions.explanation: SA 701 states that communicating KAMs is not a substitute for expressing a modified opinion. A matter giving rise to a modified opinion is by its nature a key audit matter but is reported in the Basis for Qualified/Adverse Opinion section, not in the KAM section. Other KAMs are still reported where applicable.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Neha Garments Ltd. finds that inventory is overvalued by an amount that is material but confined to inventory and not pervasive. Management refuses to correct it. The auditor should express:

options.A: A disclaimer of opinion
options.B: An unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
options.C: A qualified opinion
options.D: An adverse opinion

questions.explanation: Under SA 705, a qualified opinion is expressed when misstatements are material but not pervasive. An adverse opinion is used when misstatements are both material and pervasive. A disclaimer relates to an inability to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence where possible effects could be material and pervasive.

questions.question_text: The auditor of Om Ventures Ltd. is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence regarding receivables, inventories and investments, which together represent most of the company's total assets. The possible effects could be material and pervasive. The auditor should:

options.A: Express a qualified opinion
options.B: Disclaim an opinion
options.C: Express an adverse opinion
options.D: Express an unmodified opinion with an Other Matter paragraph

questions.explanation: SA 705 requires a disclaimer of opinion when the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and concludes that the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive. An adverse opinion is given only where the auditor has obtained evidence that misstatements exist and are material and pervasive.

questions.question_text: Under SA 705, which of the following describes effects that are 'pervasive'?

options.A: Effects that are clearly trivial but numerous
options.B: Effects that relate only to one balance sheet item
options.C: Effects that exceed performance materiality in any account
options.D: Effects that are not confined to specific elements, or if confined represent a substantial proportion of the financial statements, or relate to disclosures fundamental to users' understanding

questions.explanation: SA 705 defines pervasive effects as those that, in the auditor's judgment, are not confined to specific elements, accounts or items; or if so confined, represent or could represent a substantial proportion of the financial statements; or in relation to disclosures, are fundamental to users' understanding.

questions.question_text: After the year-end, a major earthquake damaged the main plant of Shrey Cement Ltd. Management has appropriately disclosed this in the financial statements. The auditor considers the matter fundamental to users' understanding. Under SA 706, the auditor may:

options.A: Disclaim the opinion because the full effect is unknown
options.B: Include an Emphasis of Matter paragraph referring to the disclosure, without modifying the opinion
options.C: Include an Other Matter paragraph to describe the plant's location
options.D: Qualify the opinion because of the uncertainty
